newsitem.title: CHINA: Hang Seng Index may hit 19,000 in 12 mths -Merrill.
newsitem.headline: Hang Seng Index may hit 19,000 in 12 mths -Merrill.

text.p: Merrill Lynch said liquidity flows from China could push the Hang Seng Index (HSI) above 18,000 points within 12 months, with a possible rise to 19,000 points.
"A major factor influencing the HSI...is the power of liquidity emanating, directly or indirectly, from China," Merrill Lynch said in a report dated July 15.

"Aside from the property market, key market drivers all appear positive, namely benign U.S. interest rates, a recovering PRC (People's Republic of China) economy and positive earnings momentum," it said.

Merrill Lynch said last month it expected a 10- to 15-percent correction in Hong Kong's blue-chip index, putting fair value at 13,000 points. But in its latest report, it said an almost 50 basis point contraction in the U.S. long bond yield over the last month indicated that fair value was higher at 14,125 points.
The Hang Seng Index jumped 260.27 points, or 1.69 percent, to a record closing high of 15,706.29 on Thursday. It hit an intraday record at 15,783.27 during the morning session.

"We reiterate our belief that the market is overextended in the near term and that a 10-percent correction from recent highs would still be healthy and may yet be provoked by the introduction of punitive property measures," Merrill said.
The Hong Kong government has vowed to increase housing supply to rein in rising property prices but also said it could slap punitive measures on speculators.
Merrill Lynch said the market's biggest risk was a "significant correction" in residential property prices, but it said it did not anticipate this happening.

Although Merrill predicted a 10- to 15-percent decline in residential property prices during the third quarter, it said much of the decline should already be priced into property developer stocks, which have signficantly underperformed this year.
"For the HSI to push much above its recent highs, strong performance has to come from the property and conglomerate sectors," Merrill Lynch said.
"We believe selectively both the conglomerates and property investors should perform well from here on, given their relative underperformance and attractive valuations."

Merrill adjusted its 12-month sector weightings, reducing banks to neutral from overweight, raising the overweight in conglomerates to 22 percent from 20 percent and increasing property investors to marginally overweight from neutral.
